newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends mostly up, rebound fizzles.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends mostly up, rebound fizzles.

text.p: The NYMEX electricity complex managed to finish mostly higher Tuesday when an afternoon rebound triggered by short-covering fizzled toward the close.
"It was just reflexive buying," said an East Coast electricity broker.

California-Oregon Border (COB) and Palo Verde (PV) futures fell sharply Monday on forecasts of warm weather in West and growing concerns over rising snowmelt for hydroelectric output in the Northwest.
"There wasn't much going on. It's been bits and pieces back and forth," said one Houston futures trader, noting to the lack of breadth to the brief rally.

April COB futures settled down eight cents at $10.85 a megawatt hour (MWh) after posting a high of $11.35. May COB ended down 15 cents at $9.85. Other COB months finished unchanged to 25 cents higher.
The April PV contract settled up five cents at $14.88, trimming a 52 cent gain.
May PV ended up 10 cents at $14.75. Deferred PV futures finished flat to 10 cents higher.
Day-ahead spot power prices stayed firm in Southwest with several large generating units still off-line for repairs.

Of the outages, the 1,070 megawatt (MW) San Onofre nuclear unit 2 in San Clemente, Calif., was expected to restart Thursday and reach full output this weekend. The unit has been off line since November 30 for refueling and maintenance.
The 750 MW coal-fired Four Corners unit 5 in New Mexico 750 MW was planned to resume operating Saturday after being shut a week ago for repairs.
Market sources said they are uncertain about the near direction for power futures after the choppy sessions today and yesterday.
"People will try to find a base, a bottom," said the Houston trader.
NYMEX estimated 173 COB and 276 PV lots were sold, compared with 294 COB and 275 PV lots Monday.
